extraction.name: EgoLife Dataset
extraction.description: An ultra-long, egocentric, interpersonal, multiview, multimodal daily-life dataset collected from six participants living together for seven days in Beijing, China. Approximately 300 hours were captured, with 266 hours of retained footage reported. Data include synchronized first-person and third-person recordings, sensor signals, transcripts, dense narrations, visual-audio captions, and the EgoLifeQA long-context question-answering benchmark. A separate one-day collection in Milan, Italy, is named EgoLife-Milan.
extraction.creator: The EgoLife Team
extraction.inLanguage: Primarily Chinese, with transcripts, captions, and question-answer annotations translated into English. EgoLife-Milan is primarily English, with some Chinese and Italian.
extraction.citeAs: The EgoLife Team. EgoLife: Towards Egocentric Life Assistant. arXiv:2503.03803v1 [cs.CV], 5 March 2025.
extraction.isLiveDataset: The dataset card describes EgoLife as an ongoing project.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Six volunteers lived together for seven days in a custom-designed environment called EgoHouse in Beijing, preparing an Earth Day party on the sixth day. Each wore Meta Aria glasses to capture multimodal egocentric recordings, supplemented by 15 strategically placed GoPro cameras and two mmWave radars. Activities included discussions, shopping, cooking, socializing, entertainment, rehearsals, decorating, and sightseeing. Investigators monitored participants to ensure at least six hours of recording per day and gently prompted meaningful activity during prolonged passive behavior. Recordings were collected in three-hour segments, followed by approximately one hour for upload and storage clearance. Participants were instructed to rest in their rooms during these interruptions. Filming-location permission, institutional ethics approval, and participant informed consent were obtained. A separate one-day Milan session used six Aria glasses, six indoor cameras, three mmWave radars, and WiFi devices.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Continuous capture was interrupted every three hours because of storage limitations. Glasses were collected for data upload and storage clearance, taking approximately one hour; participants were instructed to remain in their rooms and limit activity to resting or non-essential tasks during these intervals.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data came from Meta Aria glasses recording first-person video, audio, IMU, and gaze signals; GoPro cameras recording third-person video; and mmWave radar data capture boards obtaining raw ADC streams. Beijing used two TI IWR6843 60 GHz radars with DCA1000 capture boards. Milan additionally used an AWR1843 77 GHz radar and three Asus RT-AX82U devices to transmit WiFi frames and collect channel state information through the AX-CSI platform.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Faces of participants and bystanders, vehicle license plates, and sensitive visual information were blurred. Sensitive screen content, including passwords and personal data, was masked, and sensitive or potentially identifying audio was muted. Chinese annotations were translated into English.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The EgoSync codebase exported signals from Aria VRS files and synchronized Aria recordings, GoPro videos, and multimodal signals using timestamps. Cleaning removed sensitive or low-quality segments, and EgoBlur applied privacy protection. Audio was processed to mute sensitive information and enhance clarity. For transcript annotation, synchronized audio from six participants was merged into one track and subsequently separated into participant-specific tracks. For caption annotation, videos were split into five-minute clips and slowed to 0.8 times their original speed. Representative frames were sampled at one frame per second for visual-audio caption generation. Radar postprocessing used constant false alarm rate detection to identify dynamic target signals within background noise and distinguish them from static environmental signals.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Transcripts were initialized with speech recognition and open-source speaker diarization, then reviewed for accuracy. Reviewers refined six participant-specific audio tracks, retaining only speech audible to each participant and identifying each speaker. Caption annotators continuously narrated actions, interactions, environmental details, and participant focus over slowed five-minute video clips. Narration was transcribed, reviewed, corrected, and time-aligned. GPT-4o-mini merged 361K brief narration phrases into 25K coherent captions. GPT-4o combined these captions with sampled frames and transcripts to create visual-audio captions, which human annotators verified. EgoLifeQA covers EntityLog, EventRecall, HabitInsight, RelationMap, and TaskMaster. GPT-4o generated approximately 100K timestamped QA candidates per participant from visual-audio captions. Human annotators used these candidates as filtering and inspiration tools, retained questions requiring information from at least five minutes earlier, refined selected questions, authored multiple-choice distractors, and annotated audio requirements and look-back time. The final curation described in Section 3.5 produced 500 QAs per participant, totaling 3K.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: CapCut video editing software with dubbing functions was used for caption narration. SRT files displayed QA candidates in synchronization with video and supported caption alignment, review, and correction in compatible video playback software.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Automatic transcripts and diarization were reviewed and corrected by humans, including participant-specific refinement based on speech audibility. Narrations were transcribed and corrected for temporal alignment. Related phrases were consolidated with GPT-4o-mini, expanded with visual and speech context using GPT-4o, and verified by humans. AI-generated QA candidates were not treated as final annotations. Annotators preferred questions with longer temporal dependencies and strong real-world relevance, filtered approximately 100K candidates per participant to 1K for further revision, and ultimately curated 500 per participant. Questions requiring information less than five minutes earlier were excluded. Caption annotations in SRT format enabled direct video alignment and validation.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Whisper speech recognition; Whisper diarization; GPT-4o-mini for narration merging; GPT-4o for visual-audio caption expansion, QA candidate generation, and timestamped activity categorization; EgoCaption and EgoTranscript processing modules.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan to expand the dataset to additional languages, locations, and activities and encourage community contributions. The Milan collection will be detailed in an upcoming EgoLife blog series. The annotation-team partnership is intended to continue for future EgoLife versions. No update schedule or deprecation policy is specified.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Recordings contain participant and bystander faces, voices and speaker identities, daily activities, personal habits, interpersonal interactions, and spatial or movement information. Collection locations and interaction languages are documented. The privacy protocol addresses vehicle license plates, potentially identifying or private audio, and screen content containing passwords or personal data. Faces and sensitive visual information were blurred, and sensitive audio was muted to protect identities.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper describes potential benefits for personalized assistance, personal organization, contextual reminders, and quality of life, particularly for elderly people or individuals with cognitive challenges. Educational and professional applications include learning, task tracking, and skill development adapted to individual needs. Integration into personal spaces raises privacy and ethical concerns; the authors emphasize user autonomy, trust, data safeguards, and transparency in AI decision-making as essential for positive societal reception.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The authors intentionally began with a narrow setting, sacrificing some generalizability through a single language and scenario. The main dataset consists of six participants in a shared Beijing environment over seven days. Storage limitations required regular approximately one-hour recording interruptions. The paper reports approximately 300 hours collected but 266 hours retained. In this paper version, EgoLifeQA experimental evaluation was limited to Jake's 500 questions.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and fine-tuning egocentric multimodal models, including EgoGPT training on visual-audio captions and participant-specific personalization using Day-1 recordings. EgoLifeQA supports benchmark evaluation of long-context multiple-choice question answering across entity logging, event recall, habit analysis, interpersonal relationship understanding, and task tracking. Broader research uses include human behavior recognition, multimodal signal analysis, human-machine interaction, synchronized human behavior modeling, and ego-exo analysis. Intended assistant applications include finding misplaced items, recalling past events, tracking health habits, analyzing social interactions, and making personalized recommendations.
